# Opal Pettigrew

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c35 P1](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0001)</sub>
- **Status:** deceased  <sub>[v3 c11 P6](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0006), [v3 c14 P30](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0030)</sub>
- **Origin:** Brierley  <sub>[v1 c15 P39](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0039), [v3 c14 P30](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0030)</sub>
- **Role:** teacher  <sub>[v2 c19 P60](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0060), [v3 c11 P6](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0006)</sub>

## Appearance

Opal is described as a striking and extremely beautiful young woman with radiant skin, a full figure, and big, vivid blue eyes. She has a lengthy blonde plait of hair that she wears styled up while in town, sometimes adorned with red geraniums. Before her passing, her illness left her extremely slender with nearly see-through hands and feverishly flushed cheeks.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028), [v1 c30 P43](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0043), [v1 c35 P1](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0001), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v3 c2 P4](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0004), [v3 c11 P4](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0004)_

## Personality

Opal possesses a sunny, pleasant disposition and enjoys much laughter and the fun of living. She is sentimental and prone to hysteria in crises or emotional moments. Preoccupied with male attention and romantic affairs, she delights in keeping suitors dangling, though her written correspondence can be foolish and effusive.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P39](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0039), [v1 c18 P15](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0015), [v1 c21 P2](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0002), [v1 c23 P16](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0016), [v1 c26 P6](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0006), [v1 c26 P21](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0021), [v1 c35 P1](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0001), [v3 c5 P7](../source/v03-c05.md#nw-v03-c05-p0007)_

## Goals

- to keep dozens of suitors dangling and drive them wild once grown up  <sub>[v1 c18 P15](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0015), [v2 c26 P59](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0059)</sub>

## History

Opal attended Brierley school alongside Nell Harcourt, Isolde Pembroke, and Odette Pullen, where she participated in the Story Club and was known for her romantic, sentimental writing style. She went on to attend Regent’s Academy to train as a teacher, where she was considered the most beautiful girl in her year and was frequently escorted home by Hugh Carrow. After graduating, she secured a teaching position at Delford school and spent her weekends gathering with her former classmates. She accumulated numerous suitors, receiving and rejecting proposals from Nelson Atkins and the Tullyvale schoolmaster. Following a bout of congestion during the winter, Opal contracted galloping consumption, forcing her to step away from teaching, though she held onto hopes of instructing at Pale Sands school in the autumn. She spent her final summer receiving visits from friends, reconciling past school feuds, and confiding her fear of dying young and entering an unfamiliar afterlife to Nell. She passed away peacefully in her sleep shortly thereafter and was buried in Brierley cemetery.

_Sources: [v1 c26 P21](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0021), [v1 c30 P21](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0021), [v1 c35 P1](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0001), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v2 c19 P60](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0060), [v2 c26 P56](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0056), [v3 c8 P3](../source/v03-c08.md#nw-v03-c08-p0003), [v3 c11 P6](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0006), [v3 c11 P53](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0053), [v3 c12 P10](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0010), [v3 c14 P13](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0013), [v3 c14 P15](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0015), [v3 c14 P23](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0023), [v3 c14 P30](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0030), [v3 c18 P3](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0003)_

## Background by volume

- cured her warts using an enchanted stone given by old Mary Joe  <sub>[v1 c16 P18](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0018)</sub>
- had numerous older sisters who married quickly  <sub>[v1 c18 P15](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0015), [v1 c26 P17](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0017)</sub>
- hid in a hallway pantry when her sister Tabitha accepted a proposal  <sub>[v1 c26 P17](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0017)</sub>
- secured her first teaching position at the Delford school  <sub>[v2 c19 P59](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0059), [v2 c19 P60](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0060)</sub>
- sent a blistering rejection to Nelson Atkins after discovering his proposal in an etiquette guide  <sub>[v2 c26 P56](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0056)</sub>
- visited Boston during the autumn  <sub>[v3 c11 P34](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0034)</sub>

## Quotes

> Floating downward does not bother me when two or three of us are occupying the flat and we are able to sit upright. During those times, it is enjoyable. However, lying flat and acting as if I were deceased—that is something I simply could not do. Fear would actually kill me.  <sub>[v1 c28 P1](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0001)</sub>

> Oh, she appears truly deceased. It fills me with fear, girls. Is it really proper for us to perform in this manner, do you think? Mrs. Sowerby claims that any drama-acting is dreadfully sinful.  <sub>[v1 c28 P13](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0013)</sub>

> I will not be here Tuesday or Wednesday nights. A concert is taking place in Delford, followed by a gathering at Pale Sands. Herb Tranter is escorting me. He is my newest flame. Do not fail to visit me tomorrow. I am eager to have a proper conversation with you. I wish to know everything regarding your activities in Wexcombe.  <sub>[v3 c11 P8](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0008)</sub>

> Because—because—oh, Nell, I am not scared that I will fail to get into heaven. I belong to the church. But—everything there is going to be so unfamiliar. I ponder—and ponder—and it makes me so scared—and—and—homesick. Of course, heaven has to be extremely beautiful, as the Bible states—however, Nell, it will not be like what I am accustomed to.  <sub>[v3 c14 P13](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0013)</sub>

> I can’t help it. Even if what you say about heaven is true—and you can’t be sure—it may be only that imagination of yours—it won’t be just the same. It can’t be. I want to go on living here. I’m so young, Nell. I haven’t had my life. I’ve fought so hard to live—and it isn’t any use—I have to die—and leave everything I care for.  <sub>[v3 c14 P15](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0015)</sub>
